title.zh: 卷一百三十九 志第九十二 樂十四
title.raw: 卷一百三十九 志第九十二 樂十四 Volume 139 Treatises 92: Music 14

translations.literal: Music 14
translations.idiomatic: Music XIV

translations.literal: (Hymns Section Eight)
translations.idiomatic: (Section Eight: Hymns)

sentences.zh: ○恭上皇帝皇太后尊號下冊立皇后冊皇太子皇子冠鄉飲酒聞喜宴鹿鳴宴

translations.literal: ○ Ceremonial presentation of honorific titles to the emperor and empress dowager; conferring titles and investiture; installation of the empress; investiture of the crown prince; capping of imperial sons; village drinking ceremony; Court Congratulations Banquet; Deer Call Banquet
translations.idiomatic: ○ Hymns for presenting honorific titles to the emperor and empress dowager, for conferring titles and investiture, for installing the empress, for investiture of the crown prince, for the capping of imperial princes, for the village drinking ceremony, for the Court Congratulations Banquet, and for the Deer Call Banquet

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年恭上壽聖皇太后、至尊壽皇聖帝、壽成皇后尊號冊寶十四首大慶殿發冊寶降殿，《正安》帝受內禪，紀元紹熙。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, ceremonially presenting honorific titles to Empress Dowager Shousheng, the Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi, and Empress Shoucheng — fourteen hymns for the conferral of registers and seals. When the registers and seals departed Daqing Hall and descended from the hall, 《Zheng'an》: The emperor received the abdication within the palace and proclaimed the Shaoxi era.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 1, at the ceremonial presentation of honorific titles to Empress Dowager Shousheng, the Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi, and Empress Shoucheng — fourteen hymns for conferring registers and seals. As the registers and seals left Daqing Hall and the hall descent was performed, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: The emperor had received the throne by abdication and proclaimed the Shaoxi era.

translations.literal: He revered and honored his benevolent parent; with filial heart he was solemn and reverent.
translations.idiomatic: He revered his gracious parent, his filial devotion solemn and reverent.

translations.literal: Then he established illustrious titles; then he completed the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Then he raised their glorious titles; then he brought the grand rite to completion.

translations.literal: The registers were issued in the broad courtyard; songs and music assisted the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the broad courtyard the registers were proclaimed, song and music lending their aid.

sentences.zh: 中書令、侍中奉三宮冊寶詣東階下，用《禮安》鍾鼓交作，文物鹹備。

translations.literal: The Zhongshu Ling and Shizhong bore the registers and seals of the three palaces to the foot of the eastern steps, using 《Li'an》; bells and drums struck together, and ceremonial regalia were all in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat and the Palace Attendant bore the registers and seals of the three palaces to the foot of the eastern steps, to the tune 《Li'an》; bells and drums sounded together, and every ceremonial implement was in place.

translations.literal: In the vermillion court with jade steps, the Son of Heaven arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Upon vermillion court and jade steps, the Son of Heaven took his place.

translations.literal: I charge you, assisting ministers — display your offices and set each matter in order.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel, you assisting ministers: take up your duties and put every detail in its place.

translations.literal: The assisting ministers bowed to the forehead — how could they fail to lead the rites!
translations.idiomatic: The ministers bowed to the ground: how could they but conduct the ceremony!

translations.literal: As the registers and seals departed the gate, 《Zheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals left the gate, to the tune 《Zheng'an》

translations.literal: Lofty, lofty is the celestial palace; the great gates swing wide open.
translations.idiomatic: Towering stands the celestial palace; its great gates open wide.

translations.literal: Banners and pennants flourish luxuriantly; swords and girdle-pendants crowd together in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Banners and streamers billow in splendor; swords and jade pendants crowd the scene.

translations.literal: The precious registers set forth; the imperial procession followed in departure.
translations.idiomatic: The precious registers set out on their way; the imperial train followed after.

translations.literal: How brilliant is this grand ceremony — all who behold it rejoice together!
translations.idiomatic: How resplendent this grand rite — all who witness it share in its joy!

sentences.zh: 冊寶入重華宮，《正安》仰止皇居，九門載辟，麗日重光，非煙五色。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals entered Chonghua Palace, 《Zheng'an》: Looking up to the imperial residence, the nine gates were opened wide; the beautiful sun shone anew; five-colored auspicious clouds arose.
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals entered Chonghua Palace, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: Gazing up at the imperial dwelling, the nine gates stood open; the radiant sun shone again; five-colored auspicious vapors rose.

translations.literal: Like thunder the myriad chariots stirred; like clouds the hundred officials followed.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand chariots thundered forth; a hundred ranks of officials followed like clouds.

translations.literal: Within a foot of the layered heavens, they bowed and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Within a step of the highest heaven, they bowed low and held their breath.

sentences.zh: 至尊壽皇聖帝升坐，《乾安》

translations.literal: The Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi ascended to his seat, 《Qian'an》
translations.idiomatic: As the Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi took his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》

translations.literal: (Same as for descent.)
translations.idiomatic: (Same hymn as for descent.)

translations.literal: The jade seal and jasper registers — ceremonial demeanor fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: Jade seal and registers of fine jade — every detail of the rite in place.

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn is the Supreme One; in the splendid hall he takes his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and serene the Supreme Sovereign; in the splendid hall he holds court.

translations.literal: His virtue matches that of Shun of Yu; he continues Tang and confers the mandate as Yu did.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue rivals Shun of Yu; like Tang he succeeds, like Yu he passes on the mandate.

translations.literal: For ten thousand years may he receive Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: For ten thousand years may he receive Heaven's grace.

sentences.zh: 太傅、中書令奉至尊壽皇聖帝冊升殿，用《聖安》慈皇天臨，表怡怡。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor and Zhongshu Ling bore the register of the Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi up to the hall, using 《Sheng'an》: The benevolent emperor descends from Heaven; his countenance is serene and joyful.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor and Director of the Secretariat bore the Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi's register up to the hall, to the tune 《Sheng'an》: The gracious emperor comes from Heaven; his bearing is serene and glad.

translations.literal: Revered is the holy son — he personally presents the jade goblet!
translations.idiomatic: Revered is the sacred heir — he himself offers the jade cup!

translations.literal: The giant turtle dances, Mount Song resounds with acclamation — joy pervades Chinese and barbarian alike.
translations.idiomatic: The realm leaps for joy, Mount Song echoes with praise — delight fills all within the four seas.

translations.literal: The attending ministers bore the register — thus reverent, thus respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The attending ministers held the register — all reverence, all devotion.

sentences.zh: 太傅、侍中奉至尊壽皇聖帝寶升殿，用《聖安》

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor and Shizhong bore the seal of the Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi up to the hall, using 《Sheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant bore the Supreme Emperor Shouhuang Shengdi's seal up to the hall, to the tune 《Sheng'an》

translations.literal: Lofty is that splendid jade, engraved with fish and dragon knobs.
translations.idiomatic: Radiant is that fine jade, carved with fish and dragon seals.

translations.literal: Together with the register ascend; I charge you, chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ascend together with the register — counsel, you chief minister.

translations.literal: They chant it in song and verse, harmonized with drums and bells.
translations.idiomatic: They sing it in verse and song, joined with drums and bells.

translations.literal: Whether ascending or descending, none failed in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Whether they ascended or descended, none lacked reverence.

sentences.zh: 太傅、中書令、侍中奉壽聖皇太后冊寶升殿，用《聖安》

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, Zhongshu Ling, and Shizhong bore the register and seal of Empress Dowager Shousheng up to the hall, using 《Sheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, Director of the Secretariat, and Palace Attendant bore Empress Dowager Shousheng's register and seal up to the hall, to the tune 《Sheng'an》

translations.literal: Heaven blesses the imperial house; blessings gather in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blesses the royal house; joy gathers in the inner court.

translations.literal: The seal spreads the name abroad; the register transmits the glory.
translations.idiomatic: The seal proclaims the name; the register spreads the glory.

translations.literal: Golden branches flourish in splendor; the grand array displays solemn majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Golden banners shine in splendor; the grand procession shows solemn majesty.

translations.literal: He charged his close assistants to assist in the rites without deviation.
translations.idiomatic: He charged his close ministers to conduct the rites without fail.

sentences.zh: 太傅、中書令、侍中奉壽成皇后冊寶升殿，用《聖安》大哉乾元，既極形容！

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, Zhongshu Ling, and Shizhong bore the register and seal of Empress Shoucheng up to the hall, using 《Sheng'an》: Great is the Qian origin — its form has reached its utmost expression!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, Director of the Secretariat, and Palace Attendant bore Empress Shoucheng's register and seal up to the hall, to the tune 《Sheng'an》: How great is the origin of Heaven — its form has reached its fullest expression!

translations.literal: The Kun origin's virtue has reached its utmost — truly it rivals in elevation.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of Earth has reached its height — truly it rivals Heaven in grandeur.

translations.literal: Register and seal ascended together — carved in honor, glory handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Register and seal rose together — glory carved in stone, fame handed down.

translations.literal: They assisted in our elaborate rites — solemn, solemn; harmonious, harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted in our elaborate ceremony — solemn and serene, dignified and harmonious.

sentences.zh: 皇帝從壽聖皇太后冊寶詣慈福宮，用《正安》涓辰協吉，時維春元。

translations.literal: The emperor followed the register and seal of Empress Dowager Shousheng to Cifu Palace, using 《Zheng'an》: The chosen day accorded with auspiciousness; the season was the first of spring.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Empress Dowager Shousheng's register and seal to Cifu Palace, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: The chosen day was auspicious; the season was spring's beginning.

translations.literal: Registers were presented in the three halls — without precedent since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Registers were presented in the three halls — unprecedented since antiquity.

translations.literal: Striving to equal the inner palace; accumulated blessings have their source.
translations.idiomatic: Striving to match the inner court; accumulated blessings have their wellspring.

translations.literal: Thus honored, thus revered — the emperor's heart was full of devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Thus honored and revered — the emperor's heart brimmed with devotion.

sentences.zh: 壽聖皇太后出閣升坐，《坤安》

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Shousheng emerged from her pavilion and ascended to her seat, 《Kun'an》
translations.idiomatic: As Empress Dowager Shousheng came forth from her pavilion and took her seat, to the tune 《Kun'an》

translations.literal: (Same as for descent.)
translations.idiomatic: (Same hymn as for descent.)

translations.literal: Splendid and illustrious is the Song — three sages transmitted and received the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid and glorious is the Song — three sage rulers passed the mandate from hand to hand.

translations.literal: Who assisted in this?
translations.idiomatic: Who was it that aided in this?

translations.literal: It was our Great Mother.
translations.idiomatic: It was our Great Empress Mother.

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace received the register and drank this spring wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace received the register and drank this wine of spring.

translations.literal: The holy son and divine grandsons attended closely at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred heir and divine grandsons attended closely at his side.

sentences.zh: 內侍官舉壽聖皇太后冊寶詣讀冊寶位，用《聖安》

translations.literal: The inner attendants raised the register and seal of Empress Dowager Shousheng and proceeded to the reading position, using 《Sheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendants bore Empress Dowager Shousheng's register and seal to the reading position, to the tune 《Sheng'an》

translations.literal: Earth's virtue grows ever higher; Heaven's longevity is peacefully attained.
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of Earth rises ever higher; Heaven's gift of long life is peacefully received.

translations.literal: Blessings flow for ten thousand generations; descendants number in the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings flow for ten thousand generations; descendants number in the hundreds of millions.

translations.literal: Carved in jade, cast in gold — the display is brilliant and resplendent.
translations.idiomatic: Carved in jade, cast in gold — the display is magnificent and resplendent.

translations.literal: Only in antiquity were Jiang and Ren — none can match us now.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jiang and Ren of old could compare — none now can match her.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣壽成殿，壽成皇后出閣升坐，《坤安》

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to Shoucheng Hall; Empress Shoucheng emerged from her pavilion and ascended to her seat, 《Kun'an》
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Shoucheng Hall; as Empress Shoucheng came forth from her pavilion and took her seat, to the tune 《Kun'an》

translations.literal: (Same as for descent.)
translations.idiomatic: (Same hymn as for descent.)

translations.literal: She nurtured and protected — the way of the mother was fully fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: She nurtured and sheltered — the way of motherhood was complete.

translations.literal: In secret she assisted in the transmission of the throne — her virtue reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In secret she aided the transmission of the throne — her virtue reached its height.

translations.literal: In colored robes she came to court; her gracious countenance showed joy.
translations.idiomatic: In festive robes she came to court; her gracious face showed delight.

translations.literal: Having received the great name, she received yet more blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Having received the great title, she received yet more blessings.

sentences.zh: 內侍官舉壽成皇后冊寶詣讀冊寶位，用《聖安》仰瞻慈闈，登進寶冊。

translations.literal: The inner attendants raised the register and seal of Empress Shoucheng and proceeded to the reading position, using 《Sheng'an》: Looking up to the gracious inner court, they ascended and presented the precious register.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendants bore Empress Shoucheng's register and seal to the reading position, to the tune 《Sheng'an》: Gazing up at the gracious inner court, they ascended and presented the precious register.

translations.literal: At that time the inner attendants reverently performed their duties.
translations.idiomatic: At that hour the inner attendants reverently carried out their duties.

translations.literal: Both longevity and title — the mother attains both together.
translations.idiomatic: Long life and honored name — the mother receives both together.

translations.literal: She matches our honored father; for a hundred million years without end.
translations.idiomatic: She stands beside our honored father; for endless ages without limit.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年加上壽聖皇太后尊號八首大慶殿發冊寶降殿，《正安》德厚重闈，衝澹粹穆。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi, adding to the honorific title of Empress Dowager Shousheng — eight hymns. When the registers and seals departed Daqing Hall and descended from the hall, 《Zheng'an》: Virtue is deep in the inner palace; serene, pure, and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 4, at the addition to Empress Dowager Shousheng's honorific title — eight hymns. As the registers and seals left Daqing Hall and the hall descent was performed, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: Virtue runs deep in the inner court; serene, pure, and dignified.

translations.literal: By what shall we name her?
translations.idiomatic: What name shall we give her?

translations.literal: Only benevolence, only blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and blessing alone.

translations.literal: The seal carved in fine gold; the register engraved on splendid jade.
translations.idiomatic: The seal carved in fine gold; the register engraved on radiant jade.

translations.literal: Objects abundant, rites exalted — brilliantly displayed to all eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Objects in abundance, rites exalted — brilliantly displayed for all to see.

sentences.zh: 中書令、侍中奉壽聖皇太后冊寶詣東階下，《禮安》於皇帝室，休運貽孫。

translations.literal: The Zhongshu Ling and Shizhong bore the register and seal of Empress Dowager Shousheng to the foot of the eastern steps, 《Li'an》: In the emperor's house, the blessed fortune is bequeathed to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant bore Empress Dowager Shousheng's register and seal to the foot of the eastern steps, to the tune 《Li'an》: In the emperor's house, blessed fortune passes to his descendants.

translations.literal: Blessings piled upon blessings — reverently advancing the title in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings heaped upon blessings — reverently advancing the title in honor.

translations.literal: Thus is this register conferred — he must do it in person, he must do it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Thus this register is conferred — he must do it in person, with his own hands.

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven is sagely and filial — the model for ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is sage and filial — a model for all the realm.

sentences.zh: 冊寶出門，《正安》煌煌冊寶，天子受之。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals departed the gate, 《Zheng'an》: Brilliant, brilliant are the registers and seals — the Son of Heaven receives them.
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals left the gate, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: Resplendent are the registers and seals — the Son of Heaven receives them.

translations.literal: His words were measured, his steps deliberate — solemnly he displayed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: His words were measured, his steps deliberate — solemnly he performed the ceremony.

translations.literal: What is this ceremony?
translations.idiomatic: What is this ceremony?

translations.literal: Swords and girdle-pendants, yellow imperial banners.
translations.idiomatic: Swords and jade pendants, yellow imperial banners.

translations.literal: The phoenix carriage with cleared roads — all gazed up along the nine thoroughfares.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage with roads cleared — all looked up along the nine avenues.

sentences.zh: 冊寶入慈福宮殿門，《正安》

translations.literal: As the registers and seals entered the gate of Cifu Palace, 《Zheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals entered the gate of Cifu Palace, to the tune 《Zheng'an》

translations.literal: On this bright day the rites were complete — numerous and dignified, harmonious and serene.
translations.idiomatic: On this auspicious day the rites were complete — numerous and dignified, harmonious and serene.

translations.literal: Thus they bore this register to the palace of the honored parent.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they bore this register to the palace of the revered parent.

translations.literal: The palace curtains were opened wide; harmonious qi responded and connected.
translations.idiomatic: The palace curtains stood open; harmonious spirit flowed through.

translations.literal: The imperial rites were personally displayed; blessings of longevity without end.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial rites were personally performed; blessings of long life without end.

sentences.zh: 太傅、中書令、侍中奉壽聖皇太后冊寶升殿，《聖安》既肅琨庭，載升金。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, Zhongshu Ling, and Shizhong bore the register and seal of Empress Dowager Shousheng up to the hall, 《Sheng'an》: The jade courtyard was already solemn; they ascended the golden steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor, Director of the Secretariat, and Palace Attendant bore Empress Dowager Shousheng's register and seal up to the hall, to the tune 《Sheng'an》: The jade courtyard was already solemn; they ascended the golden steps.

translations.literal: They guided and they attended — majestic bearing, numerous and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: They led and they attended — majestic bearing, numerous and dignified.

translations.literal: Heaven's steps continued to arrive — filial devotion was fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's steps drew near — filial devotion was complete.

translations.literal: Voice and countenance brilliantly displayed — within and without, all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Voice and bearing brilliantly displayed — within and without, all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 冊寶詣宮中，《正安》周輿彩仗，祗詣慈宮。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals proceeded into the palace, 《Zheng'an》: The Zhou-style carriage with colored banners — reverently proceeding to the gracious palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals proceeded into the palace, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: The imperial carriage with colored banners — reverently proceeding to the gracious palace.

translations.literal: The precious register borne before; dragons flanked, clouds followed.
translations.idiomatic: The precious register borne before; dragons flanked, clouds followed.

sentences.zh: 言備茲禮，於宮之中，惟天子孝，於昭祲容。

translations.literal: Thus this rite was complete within the palace — only the Son of Heaven's filial piety brilliantly displayed his solemn bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the rite was complete within the palace — only the Son of Heaven's filial devotion brilliantly displayed his solemn bearing.

sentences.zh: 壽聖皇太后出閣升御坐，《坤安》

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Shousheng emerged from her pavilion and ascended to the imperial seat, 《Kun'an》
translations.idiomatic: As Empress Dowager Shousheng came forth from her pavilion and took the imperial seat, to the tune 《Kun'an》

translations.literal: (Same as for descent.)
translations.idiomatic: (Same hymn as for descent.)

translations.literal: The virtuous canon and great register — the displayed rites are profound and deep.
translations.idiomatic: The virtuous canon and great register — the ceremony displayed is profound and deep.

translations.literal: Serene and joyful, serene and pleased — upon the precious seat she presides.
translations.idiomatic: Serene and joyful, serene and pleased — upon the precious throne she presides.

translations.literal: In layered splendor attendants stood solemnly; deeply she displayed her reverent heart.
translations.idiomatic: In layered splendor attendants stood solemnly; deeply she showed her reverent heart.

translations.literal: The three palaces joined in celebration; forever spreading their glorious renown.
translations.idiomatic: The three palaces shared in celebration; forever spreading their glorious fame.

sentences.zh: 內侍官舉壽聖皇太后冊寶詣讀冊寶位，用《聖安》

translations.literal: The inner attendants raised the register and seal of Empress Dowager Shousheng and proceeded to the reading position, using 《Sheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendants bore Empress Dowager Shousheng's register and seal to the reading position, to the tune 《Sheng'an》

translations.literal: The precious register having been presented, reverently they recited its words.
translations.idiomatic: The precious register having been presented, reverently they recited its text.

translations.literal: Benevolence deep, blessings extending — ever more illustrious, ever more honored.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence runs deep, blessings spread wide — ever more illustrious, ever more honored.

translations.literal: Harmonious sounds and cooperative qi filled heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious sounds and cooperative spirit filled heaven and earth.

translations.literal: Together they received this blessing — the holy son and divine grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Together they received this blessing — the sacred heir and divine grandsons.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年恭上太皇太后、皇太后、太上皇帝、太上皇后尊號二十四首冊寶降殿天擁帝家，澤流子孫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan, ceremonially presenting honorific titles to the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, Retired Emperor, and Retired Empress — twenty-four hymns. As the registers and seals descended from the hall: Heaven embraces the imperial house; blessings flow to the descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 2, at the ceremonial presentation of honorific titles to the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, Retired Emperor, and Retired Empress — twenty-four hymns. As the registers and seals descended from the hall: Heaven embraces the imperial house; blessings flow to the descendants.

translations.literal: The three palaces feast together; within the four seas all pay highest honor.
translations.idiomatic: The three palaces feast together; all within the four seas pay highest honor.

translations.literal: Sounds harmonize with 《Shao》 and 《Xia》; brilliance illuminates jade and fine stone.
translations.idiomatic: Music harmonizes with 《Shao》 and 《Xia》; brilliance illuminates jade and fine gems.

translations.literal: The emperor continues in brilliant glory; his virtue shines upon heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor continues in brilliant glory; his virtue shines upon heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 冊寶授太傅奉詣東階下祖後重壽，親闈並崇。

translations.literal: The registers and seals were conferred; the Grand Tutor bore them to the foot of the eastern steps. The ancestress enjoys doubled longevity; the inner quarters are equally honored.
translations.idiomatic: The registers and seals were conferred; the Grand Tutor bore them to the foot of the eastern steps. The ancestress enjoys doubled longevity; the inner quarters are equally honored.

translations.literal: Blessings paired and felicity joined — extending the scene, spreading great glory.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings paired and felicity joined — extending the scene, spreading great glory.

translations.literal: Jade disks layered shine together; many rites brilliantly gather.
translations.idiomatic: Jade disks layered shine together; many rites brilliantly gather.

translations.literal: For hundreds of millions of years may blessings and emolument be shared alike.
translations.idiomatic: For endless ages may blessings and emolument be shared alike.

translations.literal: As the registers and seals departed the gate
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals left the gate

translations.literal: Tai Ren charmed like Jiang; Tushan aided Yu.

translations.idiomatic: Iris standards, plumed covers — guides and guards in procession.

translations.literal: Not boasting carving; not priding on elaborate splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Neither vaunting fine workmanship nor flaunting ornate display.

translations.literal: This is called the grand ceremony — billions of years, thousands of ages.
translations.idiomatic: This we name the supreme rite — to endure a billion years.

sentences.zh: 慈明殿冊寶入門金堅玉純，文鬱禮縟。

translations.literal: Ciming Palace — as the registers and seals entered the gate: gold firm, jade pure; pattern rich, rites elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: At Ciming Palace, as the registers and seals entered the gate: gold solid, jade flawless; design rich, ritual full.

translations.literal: Come from where the emperor is — making auspiciousness for the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Sent from the sovereign's hand — an omen for the realm.

translations.literal: Heaven opens, earth unfolds; sun warm, spring mild.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven opens wide, earth gives way; sunlight and spring warmth abound.

translations.literal: This is called a great affair — forever feasting on abundant emolument.
translations.idiomatic: This we call a supreme occasion — eternal peace and prosperity.

translations.literal: As the registers and seals ascended to the hall
translations.idiomatic: The registers and seals ascended to the hall

translations.literal: Imperial bearing has splendor; colorful carrying-poles rise in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The august presence shines; painted palanquins rise rank by rank.

translations.literal: Deep and still the remote hall; solemn and reverent the heavenly court.
translations.idiomatic: The lofty hall stands deep and still; the celestial court is grave and still.

translations.literal: Earthly virtue deep and elevated.
translations.idiomatic: Feminine virtue sinks deep and rises high.

translations.literal: Imperial design forever tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's charter rests secure forever.

translations.literal: I charge you court officials — gather your hem to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel, you ministers of the court: compose yourselves and ascend.

sentences.zh: 冊寶詣宮中壽為福先，明燭物表。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals proceeded into the palace: longevity is foremost of blessings; brightness illumines things above.
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals proceeded into the palace: long life leads all blessings; her radiance lights the world.

translations.literal: Benevolence touches moving things and plants; blessings equal the vaulted sky.
translations.idiomatic: Grace reaches every living thing; fortune matches the heavens.

translations.literal: Called gracious and called wise — both honorifics raised high.
translations.idiomatic: "Gracious" and "Wise" — both lofty titles now exalted.

translations.literal: Extending and declaring them — ten thousand ages eternally preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Expanding them abroad — guarded for all time.

sentences.zh: 皇太后升御坐邇臣跪奏，嚴辦必恭。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ascended to the imperial seat — nearby ministers kneel and report; solemn preparations surely reverent.
translations.idiomatic: As the Empress Dowager ascended to the imperial seat: attending ministers knelt to announce; every solemn duty performed with care.

translations.literal: Then donning ceremonial robes, ascending within the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Then arrayed in imperial robes, she mounted into the hall.

translations.literal: Gracious countenance serene and reverent; harmonious qi penetrating and blending.
translations.idiomatic: Her benevolent face tranquil and grave; gentle spirit suffusing all.

translations.literal: Fragrance flowing in clear histories — transmitted without end.
translations.idiomatic: Her fame flows through bright annals — told without end.

sentences.zh: 冊寶詣讀冊寶位徽音孔昭，寶傳斯刻。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals proceeded to the reading position: fine repute clearly displayed; treasure transmitted through this carving.
translations.idiomatic: As the registers and seals proceeded to the reading position: virtuous renown shines clear; the treasure bears these engraved words.

translations.literal: Gold bright, jade pure — brilliant is this register.
translations.idiomatic: Gold lustrous, jade flawless — radiant this sacred volume.

translations.literal: Praying and again praying — to feast and to shelter.
translations.idiomatic: We pray again and again — for peace and for protection.

translations.literal: Treasure it for ten thousand years — with Song without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Cherish it for endless years — as boundless as the Song itself.

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager descended from the imperial seat
translations.idiomatic: As the Empress Dowager descended from the imperial seat

translations.literal: Imperial text already raised; celebration rites report devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's proclamation already made; joyous rites declare sincere completion.

translations.literal: Beginning from within the palace — reaching across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From the inner palace outward — to every corner of the realm.

translations.literal: The son praises the mother's longevity; the mother calls the son worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The son proclaims his mother's long life; the mother declares her son virtuous.

translations.literal: Ascending and descending here — exalted name touching heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rising and descending in this place — her lofty title reaches the sky.

sentences.zh: 哲宗發皇后冊寶三首皇帝升坐，《乾安》

translations.literal: In the Zhezong reign, issuing the empress's registers and seals — three hymns. The emperor ascended to his seat, 《Qian'an》
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhezong reign, at the issuance of the empress's registers and seals — three hymns. As the emperor ascended to his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》

translations.literal: Having ascended, then relying — like the sun's rising.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken his place, he rests upon it — as the sun climbs the sky.

translations.literal: Stern and awe-inspiring; greatly manifest, greatly inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Majestic in discipline, strong in support; glorious to display, glorious to carry on.

translations.literal: Heaven made the union; house and state will rise.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven forged the match; family and realm flourish.

translations.literal: Cinnabar knee-covers resplendent; descendants continuous.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet regalia gleaming; offspring without end.

sentences.zh: 降坐，《乾安》我禮嘉成，我駕言旋。

translations.literal: Descending from his seat, 《Qian'an》: Our rites splendidly completed; our chariot now turns homeward.
translations.idiomatic: As he descended from his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: The ceremony stands complete; the imperial procession turns to go.

translations.literal: Descending from the seat and clearing the path, drums were struck, deep and rolling.
translations.idiomatic: As he descended from his seat and the way was cleared, drums rolled, deep and far.

translations.literal: The bright mandate has its attendant; blessing and protection come from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's bright mandate has its servants; blessing descends from on high.

translations.literal: Forever granting the heirs of the throne — how many tens of thousands of years!
translations.idiomatic: May the heirs of the throne be granted forever — for ten thousand myriad years!

sentences.zh: 太尉等奉冊寶出入，《正安》宣哲維公，就位肅莊。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal and others bore the registers and seals in and out, 《Zheng'an》: Proclaim the wise and clear lord; take your places, solemn and correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal and his colleagues bore the registers and seals in and out, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: Proclaim the wise and enlightened sovereign; take your places in solemn dignity.

translations.literal: The registers and seals were all lifted; greatly did their glory shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: The registers and seals were fully raised; their splendor shone forth.

translations.literal: Issuing from the inner palace quarters; bells and drums sounded, resonant and full.
translations.idiomatic: They issued from the imperial inner quarters; bells and drums rang out, full and resonant.

translations.literal: Motherly exemplar for all under Heaven — longevity without limit.
translations.idiomatic: As motherly exemplar to the realm — may her years know no bound.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年發皇后冊寶十三首皇帝升坐，《乾安》天地奠位，乾坤以分。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, issuing the empress's registers and seals — thirteen hymns. The emperor ascended to his seat, 《Qian'an》: Heaven and Earth were set in their places; Qian and Kun were thereby divided.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 13, at the issuance of the empress's registers and seals — thirteen hymns. As the emperor ascended to his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: Heaven and Earth took their appointed places; the roles of husband and wife were ordained.

translations.literal: Husband and wife have their distinction; father and son their mutual closeness.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife keep their proper distinction; father and son their natural bond.

translations.literal: In the governance of sage kings, ritual gives weight to marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the rule of sage kings, ritual gives marriage its due weight.

translations.literal: With proper cap and robes they undertook the affair — thus was the great human order set right.
translations.idiomatic: In proper cap and robes they performed the rite — and so the great bonds of human order were affirmed.

sentences.zh: 使副入門，《正安》天子當陽，群工就列。

translations.literal: The envoy and deputy entered the gate, 《Zheng'an》: The Son of Heaven faced the south; the host of officials took their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: As the envoy and deputy entered the gate, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: The Son of Heaven faced the south; officials of every rank took their places.

translations.literal: The registers and seals were already displayed; bells and drums were fully arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: The registers and seals had been set forth; bells and drums stood in full array.

translations.literal: The senior noble attended the affair — bearing solemn, hearts united.
translations.idiomatic: The senior duke conducted the service — grave in bearing, united in purpose.

translations.literal: Able to assist the grand rite; glory shone upon the jade register.
translations.idiomatic: They aided the grand ceremony; its brilliance lit the jade register.

translations.literal: As the registers and seals left the gate, 《Zheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals left the gate, to the tune 《Zheng'an》

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn in bearing — as when Heaven looks down.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and serene in bearing — like Heaven leaning near.

translations.literal: Brilliant and bright the clear command — like the note of jade.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and resounding the sacred charge — clear as the ring of jade.

translations.literal: Reverent and respectful as they left the gate; ritual bearing, cautious and precise.
translations.idiomatic: Devout and reverent they passed out the gate — every gesture of ritual exactingly observed.

translations.literal: At Tushan was born Qi; the Way of Xia thereby rose.
translations.idiomatic: From Tushan came Qi; by that birth the house of Xia rose.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐，《乾安》朝陽已升，薰風習至。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from his seat, 《Qian'an》: The morning sun had already risen; the balmy breeze gently arrived.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor descended from his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: The morning sun had climbed; a mild and fragrant wind came on.

translations.literal: The musical performance was finished; ritual bearing was also complete.
translations.idiomatic: The music had reached its end; every detail of ritual was in place.

translations.literal: Jade pendants chimed clearly; the emperor slowly lifted his step.
translations.idiomatic: Jade ornaments chimed as the emperor slowly raised his foot.

translations.literal: Inner governance was solemnly proclaimed, that inner administration might be heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Inner rule was proclaimed with gravity, that domestic governance might be heard.

sentences.zh: 皇后出閣，《乾安》猗歟賢後，德本性成！

translations.literal: The empress came forth from her pavilion, 《Qian'an》: Ah, the worthy consort — virtue rooted in her nature, fully formed!
translations.idiomatic: As the empress came forth from her pavilion, to the tune 《Qian'an》: Ah, the worthy empress — virtue born in her nature, fully formed!

translations.literal: She received Heaven and attained compliance; she traced the sun as her model of clarity.
translations.idiomatic: She received Heaven's charge and embodied obedience; she took the sun as her model of light.

translations.literal: Made to match the utmost pinnacle; royal transformation thereby went forth.
translations.idiomatic: Made partner at the highest pinnacle; the kingly transforming power moved through her.

translations.literal: For myriad beings, a thousand years — tending sacrifice at the ancestral shrines.
translations.idiomatic: For myriad years may she tend the ancestral shrines in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 冊寶入門，《宜安》款承祗事，時惟肅雍。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals entered the gate, 《Yi'an》: Sincerely receiving the reverent service; the moment was one of solemn harmony.
translations.idiomatic: As the registers and seals entered the gate, to the tune 《Yi'an》: With sincere reverence they undertook the service; the hour was all solemn grace.

translations.literal: Kneeling, they presented the registers and seals and displayed them at the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling, they bore the registers and seals forward and set them before the inner palace.

translations.literal: Now bowing low, now looking up — possessing both ritual and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing low and rising again — every gesture measured, every bearing correct.

translations.literal: The bright spirits interceded; fortune and emolument came in lofty measure.
translations.idiomatic: The bright spirits lent their aid; blessing and rank piled high.

translations.literal: As the empress descended from the hall, 《Cheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When the empress descended from the hall, to the tune 《Cheng'an》

translations.literal: The virtue of warmth and grace; the ceremonial robes of state.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue warm and gracious; the ceremonial robes of her rank.

translations.literal: Her conduct matched 《Caixie》; in ritual nothing was neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Her walk matched the 《Caixie》 — in ritual, not a step amiss.

translations.literal: Descending the vermillion steps — bearing and ritual in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: She descended the vermillion steps — every bearing, every gesture correct.

translations.literal: Graceful, flowing in her gait — who could match her!
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and unhurried in her bearing — who could be her like!

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊寶，《成安》鏤蒼玉兮，盛德載揚。

translations.literal: As the empress received the registers and seals, 《Cheng'an》: Carved in azure jade — great virtue, borne on high!
translations.idiomatic: When the empress received the registers and seals, to the tune 《Cheng'an》: Carved in dark jade — great virtue raised up and proclaimed!

translations.literal: Cast in southern gold — made talisman of the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Cast in southern gold — made the seal of the inner palace.

translations.literal: Reverently receiving the grant — radiant and bright!
translations.idiomatic: In reverence she received the gift — radiant, resplendent!

translations.literal: Fit for house and home — her vermillion regalia thus resplendent!
translations.idiomatic: Fit to bring harmony to the household — in scarlet regalia, truly royal!

sentences.zh: 皇后升坐，《和安》禮既行兮，厥位孔安。

translations.literal: As the empress ascended to her seat, 《He'an》: The ritual was complete — her position most secure.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress took her seat, to the tune 《He'an》: The rite was done — her place secure indeed.

translations.literal: The motherly exemplar correct — bearing and deportment fit to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: As motherly exemplar, upright — bearing and gait fit for all to witness.

translations.literal: Serving the eastern palace — always winning its delight.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the eastern court — ever bringing it joy.

translations.literal: Seeking the refined lady — is not delight of many kinds?
translations.idiomatic: Seeking the worthy lady — what delight could exceed this!

sentences.zh: 內命婦入門，《惠安》素月澄輝，眾星顯列。

translations.literal: As the inner titled ladies entered the gate, 《Hui'an》: The plain moon shed clear light; the multitude of stars stood forth in their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: As the inner titled ladies entered, to the tune 《Hui'an》: The bright moon poured clear light; the host of stars arrayed in order.

translations.literal: Brilliant as the pattern of Heaven — each with its proper station.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as the stars of Heaven — each in its appointed place.

translations.literal: The inner chambers were set right; feminine instruction was thereby established.
translations.idiomatic: The inner chambers were set in order; the woman's teaching was now established.

translations.literal: 《Guansui》 and 《Linzhi》 — they answered like an echo, swift and true.
translations.idiomatic: Like 《Guansui》 and 《Linzhi》 — their response swift as an echo.

translations.literal: As the outer titled ladies entered the gate, 《Cheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When the outer titled ladies entered the gate, to the tune 《Cheng'an》

translations.literal: Graceful and fair their countenance; virtuous and gentle their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful their looks, gentle and virtuous their bearing.

translations.literal: Brilliant as clouds they shone — gazing upon our motherly exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: Radiant as clouds they gathered — beholding our empress as motherly model.

translations.literal: Called Heaven's younger sister — in union, none more fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Called Heaven's own sister — in marriage, none more meet.

translations.literal: Brightly they danced and applauded — who did not offer reverence?
translations.idiomatic: They danced and clapped with joy — who would not bow in reverence?

sentences.zh: 皇后降坐，《徽安》寶字煌煌，冊書粲粲。

translations.literal: As the empress descended from her seat, 《Hui'an》: The characters of the treasure seal, brilliant; the register's writing, resplendent.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress descended from her seat, to the tune 《Hui'an》: The seal's characters blazed; the register's script shone.

translations.literal: Secondary hairpins added their ornament; ceremonial robes blazed with color.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary pins crowned her hair; her state robes gleamed in splendor.

translations.literal: Reverent before the emperor's favor; gracefully at ease, joyous and glad.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent before the emperor's blessing; unhurried, serene, and glad.

translations.literal: For hundreds of millions of years — forever to receive the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: For endless myriad years — forever to bear the emperor's writ.

sentences.zh: 皇帝歸閣，《泰安》太任徽音，太姒是嗣。

translations.literal: As the emperor returned to his pavilion, 《Tai'an》: Tai Ren's fine reputation — Tai Si was her successor.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor returned to his quarters, to the tune 《Tai'an》: Tai Ren's glorious fame — Tai Si followed in her line.

translations.literal: The pattern of a hundred sons — the house of Zhou thereby flourished.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred sons were her measure — the house of Zhou blazed bright.

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven — ten thousand years — receives this worthy lady.
translations.idiomatic: May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years — receiving this worthy consort.

translations.literal: As Si served Ren — followed by grandsons and sons.
translations.idiomatic: As Tai Si served Tai Ren — with grandsons and sons to follow.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年發皇后冊寶十三首皇帝升坐，《乾安》赫赫惟皇，如日之光。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi, issuing the empress's registers and seals — thirteen hymns. The emperor ascended to his seat, 《Qian'an》: Brilliant, brilliant is the emperor — like the sun's light!
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 3, at the issuance of the empress's registers and seals — thirteen hymns. As the emperor ascended to his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: Resplendent the emperor — bright as the sun!

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn is the empress — constant as the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and serene the empress — steady as the moon.

translations.literal: The ritual was performed at its proper hour; clarity shone without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The rite was accomplished in its season; radiance without bound.

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven arrived and halted — who dared not be solemn!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven took his place — who would not stand in solemn reverence!

sentences.zh: 冊寶入門，《正安》卜月惟良，練辰斯臧。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals entered the gate, 《Zheng'an》: The month divined was propitious; the day selected was auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: As the registers and seals entered the gate, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: The month divined was fair; the day chosen, blessed.

translations.literal: Ministers and officials in the court; swords and jade pendants clashed and rang.
translations.idiomatic: Officials filled the court; swords and jade ornaments chimed together.

translations.literal: Come, you Vice Director of the Secretariat — the bright command you shall bear.
translations.idiomatic: Come forward, Vice Director — you shall bear the luminous charge.

translations.literal: With virtuous bearing in ritual — let none slacken or fall short.
translations.idiomatic: With grace and ritual in your bearing — let none falter or neglect the task.

translations.literal: As the registers and seals left the gate, 《Zheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When the registers and seals left the gate, to the tune 《Zheng'an》

translations.literal: Characters carved on bamboo with fine jade knife; the treasure cast in gold.
translations.idiomatic: The text engraved on slips with jade stylus; the seal cast in gold.

translations.literal: Who holds the credentials of office?
translations.idiomatic: Who bears the staff of command?

translations.literal: At this hour, the four high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At this hour — the four chief ministers.

translations.literal: From our civil and royal virtue — reaching to solemn purity.
translations.idiomatic: From our civil attainments, reaching to sacred clarity.

translations.literal: Graceful, unhurried; graceful, unhurried — proceeding until all was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Slow and dignified, step by step — until the rite was brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐，《乾安》冊行何曏？

translations.literal: As the emperor descended from his seat, 《Qian'an》: In which direction do the registers proceed?
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor descended from his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: Whither do the registers go?

translations.literal: To the east side of the gate.
translations.idiomatic: To the eastern side of the gate.

translations.literal: Ritual complete, music complete — fans folded, the whip sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music were complete; the fans were closed and the whip cracked.

translations.literal: The emperor lifted his jade-shod step — like the turning of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raised his jeweled foot — like Heaven wheeling in its course.

translations.literal: Peace and joy to the house and the realm — for hundreds of millions of years!
translations.idiomatic: Peace for his house and realm — for endless myriad years!

sentences.zh: 皇后出閣，《坤安》椒塗蘭馭，河潤山容。

translations.literal: As the empress came forth from her pavilion, 《Kun'an》: Pepper-dust path, orchid carriage; the river's moisture, the mountain's mien.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress came forth from her pavilion, to the tune 《Kun'an》: Perfumed path and orchid carriage; gentle as river mist on a mountain's brow.

translations.literal: Secondary hairpins on her head; ceremonial robes draped her person.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary pins crowned her head; state robes clothed her form.

translations.literal: The quiet maiden, how fair — truly aiding, truly following.
translations.idiomatic: The serene maiden, how fair — ever aiding, ever attending.

translations.literal: From that western pavilion — forthwith to the central hall.
translations.idiomatic: From the western pavilion she came — straightway into the central hall.

sentences.zh: 冊寶入門，《宜安》德隆位尊，禮厚文縟。

translations.literal: As the registers and seals entered the gate, 《Yi'an》: Virtue lofty, position honored; ritual rich, brocade of text ornate.
translations.idiomatic: As the registers and seals entered the gate, to the tune 《Yi'an》: Virtue exalted, rank supreme; ritual weighty, ornament rich.

translations.literal: Then they engraved the gold; then they carved the jade.
translations.idiomatic: They engraved the gold; they carved the jade.

translations.literal: The host of nobles filled the gate; those on duty were solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles crowded the gate; every attendant grave and correct.

translations.literal: We pray to keep it secure — forever to anchor the earth's axis.
translations.idiomatic: We pray to keep it safe — forever to steady the realm's foundation.

translations.literal: As the empress descended from the hall, 《Cheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When the empress descended from the hall, to the tune 《Cheng'an》

translations.literal: The great hall, deep and still; harmonious qi, patterns unfolding.
translations.idiomatic: The great hall stood deep and still; harmony breathed through every ornament.

translations.literal: Brightly displayed the wife's obedience — showing forth and rectifying human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly shown was wifely duty — marking and righting the bonds of humankind.

translations.literal: Treading the left steps — arriving at the central courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: She mounted the left steps — and came to the central courtyard.

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Attendants displayed her aid — none who did not show reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The chief palace lady directed the rite — none present but bowed in reverence.

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊寶，《成安》備物典冊，樂之鼓鍾。

translations.literal: As the empress received the registers and seals, 《Cheng'an》: The ritual objects and canonical registers prepared — music of drums and bells for them.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress received the registers and seals, to the tune 《Cheng'an》: Regalia and canonical registers made ready — drums and bells to honor them.

translations.literal: Bowing, she received them — utmost solemn harmony.
translations.idiomatic: She bowed and received them — in utmost solemn grace.

translations.literal: The officers of speech and of the seal — each followed according to duty.
translations.idiomatic: The keepers of the words and of the seal — each did service as his office required.

translations.literal: Upon the earth there was rejoicing; with Heaven, endless duration.
translations.idiomatic: The earth rejoiced beneath her; with Heaven her blessing knows no end.

sentences.zh: 皇后升坐，《和安》容典既膺，壺儀既正。

translations.literal: As the empress ascended to her seat, 《He'an》: Rites of bearing already received; inner ritual already set right.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress took her seat, to the tune 《He'an》: The rites of deportment were hers; the inner law was set aright.

translations.literal: Feathered guards arrayed outside; glory on her face, reflected at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Armed guards lined the outer ranks; radiance on her face, mirrored at the hall's heart.

translations.literal: Like the emperor, like Heaven — with solemnity, with splendor.
translations.idiomatic: She stood as august as the Son of Heaven, as radiant as the sky — grave and glorious.

translations.literal: The six palaces received the model; 《Ernan》 flowed in song.
translations.idiomatic: The six palaces took her as their model; hymns of 《Eranan》 rang through the court.

sentences.zh: 內命婦入門，《惠安》《葛覃》節用，《樛木》逮下。

translations.literal: As titled consorts of the inner court entered, 《Huian》: “《Ge Tan》” — thrift in practice; “《Jiaomu》” — reaching down to those below.
translations.idiomatic: As inner-court consorts entered the gate, to the tune 《Huian》: The thrift of “《Ge Tan》”; the care for subordinates of “《Jiaomu》.”

translations.literal: In bearing she was the standard for consorts; long since had hearts been transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Her bearing set the rule for palace ladies; hearts had long been won to her virtue.

translations.literal: Now presiding over Changqiu — thereby rectifying all Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Now she took her seat in the Palace of Long Autumn — and set all the realm in order.

translations.literal: With celebration, with prayer — a hundred auspices came to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: In joy and in prayer, a hundred blessings came to meet her.

translations.literal: As consorts of the outer court entered, 《Xian'an》
translations.idiomatic: As outer-court consorts entered the gate, to the tune 《Xian'an》

translations.literal: Tall and stately the lady — a wife of duke or marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Stately and tall she stood — a duchess, a marquise.

translations.literal: Pheasant-embroidered canopies for the audience — elephant-hued robes were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: With pheasant canopies she came to court; robes of ceremonial hue became her well.

translations.literal: Like stars gathering together; like the moon's reflected brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Like stars that cluster as one; like light cast back from the moon.

translations.literal: The motherly exemplar already gazed upon — all hearts were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Once her motherly bearing was seen, every heart was set at ease.

sentences.zh: 皇后降坐，《徽安》窈窕淑女，備六服兮。

translations.literal: As the empress descended from her seat, 《Huian》: “Graceful, modest lady — complete in the six garments!”
translations.idiomatic: When the empress left her seat, to the tune 《Huian》: “Fair and modest lady — robed in all six regalia!”

translations.literal: Ascending and descending — many rites; lifting every eye!
translations.idiomatic: In rise and descent, rite upon rite — every eye was raised to her!

translations.literal: Inner governance truly complete; yin instruction solemn!
translations.idiomatic: Inner rule was fully wrought; the women's code stood firm!

translations.literal: Fitting for lord and king — ease and blessing!
translations.idiomatic: Fit companion to her lord and king — peace and blessing hers!

sentences.zh: 皇后歸閣，《泰安》天監有周，是生太任。

translations.literal: As the empress returned to her pavilion, 《Taian》: “Heaven watched over Zhou; from it was born Tai Ren.”
translations.idiomatic: When the empress withdrew to her pavilion, to the tune 《Taian》: “Heaven oversaw Zhou and gave it Tai Ren.”

translations.literal: There was also Tai Si — inheriting her fine renown.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Si too arose — heir to that noble fame.

translations.literal: Who could match the Two Palaces — loving kindness succeeding one another!
translations.idiomatic: What match is there to the Two Palaces — mercy handed down in turn!

translations.literal: The greatness of “Si Qi” — again seen in this day!
translations.idiomatic: The glory of “emulation of worth” — shines again in our time!

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年皇后冊寶十三首皇帝升坐，《乾安》乾位既正，坤斯順承。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chunxi, empress registers and seals — thirteen hymns. The emperor ascended to his seat, 《Qian'an》: The Qian position was already set right; Kun thereby yielded in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 16, at the issuance of the empress's registers and seals — thirteen hymns. As the emperor took his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: The throne of Heaven was set aright; Earth bowed in dutiful accord.

translations.literal: The sun splendid upon Heaven; the moon thereby rose, bright.
translations.idiomatic: The sun blazed in the sky; the moon shone forth in answer.

translations.literal: Only the emperor received the mandate; only the emperor ascended together.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven received Heaven's charge; the imperial pair rose as one.

translations.literal: At the brocaded screen, honored presence — the canonical registers were carried forth.
translations.idiomatic: Before the brocaded screen he took his honored seat; the canonical registers were borne forward.

sentences.zh: 冊寶入門，《正安》乃協良辰，維春之宜。

translations.literal: As registers and seals entered the gate, 《Zheng'an》: Then harmonized the auspicious day — for spring it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When registers and seals were brought within, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: The auspicious day was chosen — spring's own season.

translations.literal: Then he decreed the near ministers — “Come, assist the ceremony for you.”
translations.idiomatic: He charged his closest aides — “Come, join and guide this rite.”

translations.literal: The nine gates opened wide; ritual objects and pattern, splendid glory.
translations.idiomatic: All nine gates swung wide; regalia gleamed in splendor.

translations.literal: Sonic poetry was borne in song — thereby to assist the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns were sung aloud — to grace the ceremony.

translations.literal: As registers and seals went out the gate, 《Zheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When registers and seals were borne forth, to the tune 《Zheng'an》

translations.literal: There were seals cast in gold; registers carved in jasper.
translations.idiomatic: Seals were cast of gold; registers were carved in fine jade.

translations.literal: “You envoys, you deputies — bear the credentials as you go.”
translations.idiomatic: “You envoys and deputies — go forth bearing the imperial warrant.”

sentences.zh: 禮始文德，達於穆清，是恪是虔，依我和聲。

translations.literal: Rites began with civil virtue; reached to deep purity — such reverence, such devotion; follow our harmonious music.
translations.idiomatic: The rite began in civil grace and rose to solemn clarity — devout and dutiful, they kept to the harmonious song.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐，《乾安》鼓鍾喤々，磬筦鏘鏘。

translations.literal: As the emperor descended from his seat, 《Qian'an》: Drums and bells, resonant and full; stone chimes and flutes, ringing and clear.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor left his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: Drums and bells rolled full and deep; chimes and pipes rang clear.

translations.literal: Swords and girdle-pendants filled the court — numerous and grand.
translations.idiomatic: Sword and pendant filled the hall — a host splendid and vast.

translations.literal: The ritual canon was reported complete; the imperial heart joyful and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual was proclaimed complete; the emperor's heart knew joy and ease.

translations.literal: For ten thousand such years — receiving blessing without bound.
translations.idiomatic: For ten thousand years — blessing without end.

sentences.zh: 穆清殿受冊寶，皇后出閣，《坤安》懿範柔容，如月斯輝。

translations.literal: At Hall of Deep Purity, receiving registers and seals — as the empress came forth from her pavilion, 《Kun'an》: Fine model, gentle bearing — like the moon, its radiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hall of Deep Purity she received the registers and seals; as the empress emerged from her pavilion, to the tune 《Kun'an》: A gentle, perfect bearing — bright as the moon.

translations.literal: She mounted her pheasant carriage; clad in ceremonial robes.
translations.idiomatic: She rode the pheasant-adorned carriage, dressed in sacred robes.

translations.literal: Nine palanquins followed her — like clouds, dense and even.
translations.idiomatic: Nine attendant carriages trailed her — thick as clouds, serene and slow.

translations.literal: The canonical registers she received — in heart, solemn reverence.
translations.idiomatic: She received the canonical registers — her heart steeped in reverence.

sentences.zh: 冊寶入門，《宜安》華榱璧璫，有馨椒殿。

translations.literal: As registers and seals entered the gate, 《Yian》: Splendid rafters, jade finials — fragrance in the Pepper Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When registers and seals came within, to the tune 《Yian》: Glorious beams, jade ornament — sweet fragrance in the Pepper Hall.

translations.literal: Prepared objects came set forth — many rites, brilliant display.
translations.idiomatic: Regalia was arrayed before her; ceremony after ceremony blazed bright.

translations.literal: “Thus the register, thus the seal” — carved and engraved.
translations.idiomatic: Register and seal alike — each cut and inscribed with care.

translations.literal: Together raised and carried forth — august the splendid canon!
translations.idiomatic: Borne up together in procession — how grand the hallowed rite!

translations.literal: As the empress descended from the hall, 《Chengan》
translations.idiomatic: When the empress descended from the hall, to the tune 《Chengan》

translations.literal: Ceremonial robes in full — her bearing marked by reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In her richest robes she stood — every gesture grave and correct.

translations.literal: Whether ascending or descending — attended by the Director of Palace Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Whether she climbed or came down, palace ladies guided her way.

translations.literal: Golden hall, jade steps — thus she came to the center.
translations.idiomatic: Past golden hall and jade steps, she came to the hall's heart.

translations.literal: The hymns were spread forth, matching the pitch — laden with chants, solemn and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Hymns unfolded to the measure; songs rose, solemn and sweet.

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊寶，《成安》帝有顯命，稟於親慈。

translations.literal: As the empress received registers and seals, 《Chengan》: The emperor had a clear mandate, received from his parent's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress received registers and seals, to the tune 《Chengan》: The Son of Heaven bore Heaven's charge, handed down in his elders' love.

translations.literal: The empress's virtue could receive it — bowing, she accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Her virtue was fit to bear it — she bowed and received them.

translations.literal: Human relations already rectified — royal transformation was the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Once human bonds were set right, royal order had its root.

translations.literal: For a hundred million myriad years — eternal blessing to the earth's ritual.
translations.idiomatic: For ages beyond count — everlasting grace to the empress's throne.

sentences.zh: 皇后升坐，《和安》帝慶三宮，膺受寶冊。

translations.literal: As the empress ascended to her seat, 《Hean》: The emperor celebrated the Three Palaces; received and bore the treasure registers.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress took her seat, to the tune 《Hean》: The emperor rejoiced for the Three Palaces; she received the precious registers.

translations.literal: Presiding in the inner quarter — bearing joy, bearing caution.
translations.idiomatic: She held court in the inner palace — joyous yet watchful.

translations.literal: Thus showing true yin instruction; thus clarifying 《Neize》.
translations.idiomatic: Thus she embodied the women's teaching; thus she made bright the 《Inner Rites》.

translations.literal: Careful care, fish strung in file — none who did not follow the model.
translations.idiomatic: Line upon line like swimming fish — none but followed her rule.

sentences.zh: 內命婦入門，《惠安》掖庭頒官，於位有四。

translations.literal: As inner-court consorts entered, 《Huian》: In the rear palace offices were posted — four ranks in place.
translations.idiomatic: As inner consorts entered, to the tune 《Huian》: The rear palace named its offices — four ranks arrayed.

translations.literal: “Dim are those lesser stars” — soothed with virtue and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: “Small stars, faint in the sky” — she comforted all with grace and mercy.

translations.literal: Flourishing like spring; nurturing like the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Warm as spring she shone; broad as earth she nurtured.

translations.literal: The celebration rite was completed — none who was not altogether joyful.
translations.idiomatic: The rejoicing rite was done — every heart shared the joy.

translations.literal: As consorts of the outer court entered, 《Xian'an》
translations.idiomatic: As outer-court consorts entered the gate, to the tune 《Xian'an》

translations.literal: Fish-barque carriage came at the apex — elephant-hued robes were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Her carriage came in stately state; ceremonial robes suited her well.

translations.literal: Ranked in the inner court — leading rites with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: They took their places in the inner court, devout in every observance.

translations.literal: Transformed by the woman's Way; at this time, the motherly exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: Shaped by wifely duty, she was the realm's motherly model.

translations.literal: This celebration, this gathering — all together joyful!
translations.idiomatic: In feast and in fellowship — all rejoiced as one!

sentences.zh: 皇后降坐，《徽安》正位長秋，容典備矣。

translations.literal: As the empress descended from her seat, 《Huian》: The correct seat in Changqiu — deportment canon complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress left her seat, to the tune 《Huian》: Her throne in Long Autumn was set; every rite of bearing fulfilled.

translations.literal: The king dwelt in his household — human relations at their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The king had his household in order — bonds of kin at their height.

translations.literal: Paired at the summit, equal to Heaven — many blessings received!
translations.idiomatic: Matched at the zenith, peer to Heaven — blessings poured upon her!

translations.literal: “Diligent diligent, the locust swarm” — fit for sons and grandsons!
translations.idiomatic: “Teeming locusts, gathering thick” — may sons and grandsons thrive!

sentences.zh: 皇后歸閣，《泰安》維天佑宋，盛事相仍。

translations.literal: As the empress returned to her pavilion, 《Taian》: “Only Heaven blesses Song — great affairs succeeding one another.”
translations.idiomatic: When the empress withdrew to her pavilion, to the tune 《Taian》: “Heaven blesses Song; glorious deeds follow in train.”

translations.literal: Exalted titles for the Three Palaces — just now this double festival day.
translations.idiomatic: Honored names for the Three Palaces — the very day of joint celebration.

translations.literal: For the first time rectifying the inner quarter — layered rites were set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace was first set in order; ceremony upon ceremony was displayed.

translations.literal: The rejoicing of state and clan — unmatched since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: A joy for realm and house beyond anything of old.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升坐，《乾安》乾健坤順，群生首資。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended to his seat, 《Qian'an》: Qian vigorous, Kun obedient — all living things chiefly depend on them.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor took his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: Heaven strong, Earth yielding — all creation looks to them first.

translations.literal: The sun constant, the moon rising — four seasons, leaves flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun by day, moon ascending — the four seasons flourish in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝嗣天曆，後崇母儀，黼黻承暉，王化是基。

translations.literal: The emperor succeeds Heaven's cycle; the empress honors motherly exemplar — brocaded splendor receives the light; royal transformation is the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inherits Heaven's calendar; the empress exalts motherly rule — splendor catches the light; on this royal order is founded.

translations.literal: Envoys and deputies entered the gate, 《Zheng'an》
translations.idiomatic: When envoys and deputies entered the gate, to the tune 《Zheng'an》

translations.literal: Blazing gate-towers, coiling cicada ornaments; jade gates, cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Flame-hued towers, canopies coiled like cicada wings; jade gates arrayed with cloud and dragon.

translations.literal: Illustrious pattern, assisting ministers — aiding and upholding dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers bold in civic grace upheld her with reverent mien.

translations.literal: Canons and regulations, radiant and bright; constant measures, solemn and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes blazed clear; enduring norms stood solemn and sweet.

translations.literal: Completing the season's layered rites — ascending to the jade palace.
translations.idiomatic: The season's layered rites fulfilled, she mounted to the jade hall.

sentences.zh: 冊寶出門，《正安》金晶麗輝，璧葉含春。

translations.literal: As registers and seals went out the gate, 《Zheng'an》: Golden splendor, beautiful brilliance; jade disks and leaves holding spring.
translations.idiomatic: When registers and seals were borne forth, to the tune 《Zheng'an》: Gold flashed bright; jade discs and fronds brimmed with spring.

translations.literal: Praising the assistants of Xia; continuing the consorts of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: They hymned the aides of Xià; they followed the brides of Yú.

translations.literal: Music arranged according to 《Shao》, clear; ritual pattern, ornament new.
translations.idiomatic: Music kept to the 《Shao》; ritual text, fresh as brocade.

translations.literal: Marquises and dukes completed one another; objects and pattern, refined and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Lords noble and great joined as one; regalia shone in ordered splendor.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐，《乾安》帟旒雲舒，金秀充庭。

translations.literal: As the emperor descended from his seat, 《Qian'an》: Curtain-veils and tassels like clouds unfolding; golden splendor filling the court.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor left his seat, to the tune 《Qian'an》: Curtains and tassels spread like clouds; gold gleamed throughout the hall.

translations.literal: Jade chariots and golden splendor; cinnabar pendants, tassels hanging down displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Jeweled guards and gilded splendor; scarlet girdles, pendants swaying in show.

translations.literal: Imperial bearing joyful and complete; gentle ceremony yielded in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Royal grace shone full; gentle rites followed in turn.

translations.literal: Three palaces together rejoicing — myriad blessings clearly received.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Palaces rejoiced as one — ten thousand blessings manifest upon them.

sentences.zh: 皇后出閣，《坤安》驂翟崇容，禕鞠陳衣。

translations.literal: As the empress came forth from her pavilion, 《Kun'an》: Triple pheasant teams, exalted bearing; sacred robes laid out.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress left her pavilion, to the tune 《Kun'an》: Pheasant carriages, stately train; sacred garments displayed.

translations.literal: She halted at the orchid hall; early risen from the pepper inner court.
translations.idiomatic: She reached the orchid hall, risen at dawn from the pepper quarters.

translations.literal: Pure and correct, proclaiming splendor — refined clarity soaring in brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and upright, she showed forth glory — lucid grace mounting in light.

translations.literal: Reverently responsive — heir to fine fame's emblem.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent and responsive, she bore the seal of noble lineage.

translations.literal: As registers and seals entered the gate, 《Yian》
translations.idiomatic: When registers and seals came within, to the tune 《Yian》

translations.literal: Sacred curtains, flowing light — celebratory auspice ever spreading.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred canopies shed flowing light; blessings piled ever higher.

translations.literal: Jade strung together, virtue engraved; dragon gold overflowing with seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Jade plates bound, virtue carved; dragon gold brimmed with seal script.

translations.literal: Pure counsels, embroidered splendor — emblem-text splendid and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Pure wisdom, broidered glory — emblems of grace shone clear.

translations.literal: The sonic poetry of 《Ernan》 — at this time brightly expounded.
translations.idiomatic: The hymns of 《Eranan》 — in this hour were proudly proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 皇后降殿，《承安》翬珩煥采，趨節風韶。

translations.literal: As the empress descended from the hall, 《Chengan》: Kingfisher finials, brilliant colors; keeping pace to wind and 《Shao》.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress left the hall, to the tune 《Chengan》: Kingfisher pendants flashed; she kept step to wind and sacred song.

translations.literal: Ascending and descending the terrace steps — bearing and offering splendid jade.
translations.idiomatic: Up and down the terrace steps, she bore the finest jade.

translations.literal: The cleared path received the incense; consortly rites raised their crests.
translations.idiomatic: Along the sacred way incense rose; palace grace shone forth on high.

translations.literal: Such reverence, such devotion — her virtuous fame greatly bright.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent and devout she stood — her virtue's fame shone clear.

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊寶，《成安》帝奉太室，後儀成之。

translations.literal: As the empress received registers and seals, 《Chengan》: The emperor served the Grand Chamber; the empress's ritual completed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress received registers and seals, to the tune 《Chengan》: The emperor honored the Grand Chamber; the empress's rite brought it to fulfillment.

translations.literal: The emperor nurtured the Three Palaces; the empress's record received it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sustained the Three Palaces; the empress's charge carried it on.

translations.literal: Virtue like 《Guan Ju》; abundance like 《Zhongsi》.
translations.idiomatic: Her virtue matched 《Guan Ju》; her fruitfulness, 《Zhongsi》.

translations.literal: Fitting for lord and king — a hundred ages, root and branch.
translations.idiomatic: Fit for lord and king — for a hundred generations, root and branch.

sentences.zh: 皇后升坐，《和安》肅肅壼彝，雍雍陰教。

translations.literal: As the empress ascended to her seat, 《Hean》: Solemn, solemn the inner law; harmonious, harmonious the yin teaching.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress took her seat, to the tune 《Hean》: Grave and steady the inner rule; gentle and full the women's teaching.

translations.literal: Perversity and slander she guarded against herself; vigilance was what she emulated.
translations.idiomatic: She guarded herself against deceit; watchfulness was her model.

translations.literal: In the inner quarter, bearing composed — the ranks of attendants all reported.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in the inner court, she presided; every rank of attendants made report.

translations.literal: Her thought was to assist and yield — forever to wing the emperor's filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Her mind was to aid and obey — ever to uphold the emperor's filial duty.

translations.literal: As inner-court consorts entered, 《Huian》
